findings.title: `prisma` is used but never imported, so every Salesforce calendar operation fails
findings.body: The new token-refresh code calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` inside `getClient`, but the file's import block (lines 1-20) never imports `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma`. This is a ReferenceError at runtime and a TypeScript compile error. `getClient` is invoked from the constructor and its promise is stored in `this.conn`, which create, update, delete and contact lookup all await, so those operations reject once this lands.

findings.title: Salesforce token is refreshed on every service construction, bypassing the sync endpoint
findings.body: Previously constructing the service made no network call. Now `getClient` always POSTs to login.salesforce.com and writes the credential row back, even when the stored access token is still valid. CalendarService instances are created per availability check, booking and settings page, so this adds a Salesforce login request and a DB write each time, which can run into Salesforce login rate limits. The refresh also does not go through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so with app-credential sync enabled Cal.com still refreshes with its own consumer secret instead of the self-hoster's endpoint, contrary to the purpose of this PR. The `response.statusText !== "OK"` check is also fragile (HTTP/2 responses carry no reason phrase) and discards the error body.

findings.title: Sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, but every caller reads a parsed token payload
findings.body: In sync mode the function returns the `fetch` Response from the self-hoster endpoint without parsing it or checking `response.ok`. The local branch returns an object with `.data` (Google, zohocrm, zoho-bigin) or token fields (HubSpot). Callers therefore break in sync mode: Google reads `res?.data` (undefined), so `token.access_token` throws inside a catch that silently keeps the expired access token. zoho-bigin reads `tokenInfo.data.error` outside any try block, so a TypeError propagates and every call fails. zohocrm reads `.data.error` inside its try, so the refresh is skipped with only a log line. HubSpot reads `expiresIn` and `accessToken` from it. The `() => any` signature hides this from the type checker. The sync branch should `await response.json()`, check status, and return the body in the same shape as the local branch.

findings.title: HubSpot refresh in sync mode writes a fetch Response object into the credential key
findings.body: With sync enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a fetch Response, so `hubspotRefreshToken` is a Response. `expiresIn` is undefined, so `expiryDate` becomes NaN on line 192. Line 198 then stores that Response as the credential `key`. Serialized, it becomes an empty object or Prisma rejects it, so the stored access and refresh tokens are lost. `hubspotClient.setAccessToken(hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken)` then receives undefined. The error is swallowed by the surrounding catch, so the failure is not visible.

findings.title: Placeholder 'refresh_token' value overwrites the real refresh token
findings.body: When the refresh response has no refresh_token, this sets it to the literal string 'refresh_token'. Callers persist the parsed data, so the real stored refresh token is replaced. Office365 calendar merges `tokenResponse.data` over the stored credential, so a Microsoft refresh response without refresh_token overwrites the real one, and the next refresh fails with invalid_grant. In sync mode this placeholder is produced on every refresh, because the minimum schema strips refresh_token (see line 8). The function should leave the field undefined and let callers keep the stored token.

findings.title: Minimum token schema uses computed keys that stringify to '[object Object]'
findings.body: `z.string().toString()` does not produce a key pattern. ZodType has no custom toString, so both computed keys become the literal property name '[object Object]', and the second overrides the first. The schema therefore validates only access_token, and the comment's rule that numeric properties are expiry is never enforced. Because z.object strips unknown keys by default, refresh_token, expires_in, scope and expiry_date are removed from the parsed data in sync mode. Callers then persist a key without its expiry, and Office365 keeps the old expires_in, so the token is treated as expired and refreshed on every call.

findings.title: Sync-mode condition does not match refreshOAuthTokens, corrupting team credential refreshes
findings.body: This branch uses the minimum schema whenever sync is enabled and the endpoint is set. `refreshOAuthTokens` only uses the endpoint when `userId` is also set (its line 5). For team credentials (userId null) the refresh runs locally and returns the real provider payload, but this function still applies the minimum schema. Fields are stripped and the placeholder refresh token from line 26 is written, so with sync enabled every refresh of a team credential (for example Google Calendar) corrupts the stored key. The two conditions must match, or the decision should be passed in explicitly.

findings.title: Helper now throws instead of returning a result, making caller success checks dead code
findings.body: The function previously returned the safeParse result, and callers checked `.success`. It now throws on failure, so the `.success` branches are unreachable: Office365 calendar's `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data`, zoomvideo's `if (!parsedToken.success)`, and salesforce's `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)`. Office365 also lost the console.error that logged the Zod error and the Microsoft response body. Either document the new contract and clean up the callers, or keep returning the result.

findings.title: Sync request sends app slug 'zoomvideo' while Zoom credentials are stored under 'zoom'
findings.body: The refresh call passes 'zoomvideo' as the app slug, but the Zoom callback creates credentials with `appId: "zoom"` (zoomvideo/api/callback.ts line 73) and looks them up by appId 'zoom'. The self-hoster's sync endpoint keys tokens by app slug, so a request for 'zoomvideo' will not find the Zoom token. The slug should match the credential's appId.

findings.title: Shared webhook secret compared with non-constant-time !==
findings.body: The webhook secret is compared with `!==`, which returns early on the first differing byte, so response timing can reveal how much of the secret matched. This endpoint authenticates requests that create and overwrite credentials for any user. The comparison should use crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers.

findings.title: Malformed input produces 500 errors instead of 400
findings.body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError on an invalid body rather than returning 400. Likewise `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` at line 57 throws on a wrong key or corrupt ciphertext. Neither is caught, so the handler returns 500. Wrap both and return 400 with a generic message, so a sender can distinguish a bad payload from a server fault.

findings.title: findFirst followed by create is a check-then-act race that can create duplicate credentials
findings.body: The handler reads with findFirst and then creates or updates. The schema does not enforce uniqueness on (userId, appId), as the Lark callback comment notes. Two concurrent deliveries for the same user and app (for example sender retries) can both see no row and both create one. Later lookups then act on an arbitrary duplicate.

findings.title: Sync update replaces the key but does not clear the invalid flag
findings.body: Refresh failures set `invalid: true` on the credential (for example invalid_grant in the Google, Webex and Zoom adapters). This update replaces `key` with fresh tokens but leaves `invalid` as is. A credential that was flagged invalid will keep the flag after a successful sync, so it stays excluded even though it now holds valid tokens. The update should also reset `invalid`.

findings.title: New credential-writing endpoint and sync refresh path have no tests
findings.body: The PR adds an endpoint that writes credentials for any user and a new token-refresh branch in several adapters, with no tests (the PR checklist says so). The bugs found in this change, such as the missing prisma import, the placeholder refresh token, the broken minimum schema and the sync response shape, are the kind unit tests on parseRefreshTokenResponse, refreshOAuthTokens and this handler would catch. At minimum cover: invalid secret returns 403, malformed body returns 400, create versus update, and each provider's sync-mode response handling.

findings.title: Comment understates the response shape the sync endpoint must return
findings.body: The comment says the response 'should only contain the access token and expiry date'. Callers need more: parseRefreshTokenResponse expects refresh_token, the Webex and Zoom schemas require refresh_token, scope and token_type, Lark reads refresh_expires_in, and HubSpot reads expiresIn. Self-hosters following this comment will build endpoints that fail. The documented contract, including that the body is JSON in the same shape as the provider's response, should be stated accurately.
